title: Matsumoto vs Nagano: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: Matsumoto for city culture, food, and cherry blossoms. Nagano for snow monkeys, regional base, and Zenkoji Temple. Do both — they're only 50 minutes apart.

categories.name: City Vibe & Walkability
categories.summary: Matsumoto is more compact and walkable with a great neighborhood feel. Nagano is more spread out.

categories.name: Signature Attraction
categories.summary: Matsumoto Castle vs Zenkoji Temple — both are world-class, just very different.

categories.name: Food Scene
categories.summary: Matsumoto has excellent soba, craft beer, and the Nakamachi dining district.

categories.name: Snow Monkey Access
categories.summary: Jigokudani is 90 min from Nagano Station vs 2.5 hrs from Matsumoto.

categories.name: Transit from Tokyo
categories.summary: Nagano 90 min by Shinkansen vs Matsumoto 2.5 hrs by Azusa Express.

categories.name: Kamikochi Access
categories.summary: Kamikochi is 1.5 hrs by bus from Matsumoto, significantly closer than from Nagano.

categories.name: Ski Resort Access
categories.summary: Hakuba (90 min), Shiga Kogen (60 min), Nozawa Onsen (90 min) — all much closer to Nagano.

categories.name: Cherry Blossoms
categories.summary: Matsumoto Castle + sakura + moat reflection is one of Japan's most iconic spring scenes.

categories.name: Arts & Museums
categories.summary: Matsumoto has Yayoi Kusama museum, Japan Ukiyo-e Museum, and City Museum of Art.

faq.question: Should I use Matsumoto or Nagano as a base?
faq.answer: Nagano for snow monkeys, Togakushi, and ski resorts. Matsumoto as a standalone city destination. Many travelers do 1 night Matsumoto + 2–3 nights Nagano.

faq.question: How far is Matsumoto from Nagano?
faq.answer: 45–60 minutes by train (¥670). Easy to visit both in one trip.
